config.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair

personas.name: Esther
personas.goals: A fair process and no shouting
personas.hidden_agenda: Founded the garden and finds change hard

personas.name: Dmitri
personas.goals: Get the drip system installed this year
personas.hidden_agenda: Already got a second quote he hasn't shared

personas.name: Bao
personas.hidden_agenda: Thinks the volunteer-hours rule is unfair to shift workers

agenda.title: Plots
agenda.goal: Fill the vacant plots from the waitlist

agenda.title: Irrigation
agenda.goal: Decide whether to install the drip system

agenda.title: Volunteer hours
agenda.goal: Agree what happens when people don't do their hours

facts.statement: Required volunteer hours = 8 per plot holder
Plot holders who completed their hours last year = 64%

beats.summary: Vacant plots and the waitlist; Bao overstates the waitlist
The drip system; Dmitri's quote figure is low and nobody notices
Vendors and layout; Holly's vendor count is corrected later; a tangent about the mayoral debate
The hours rule; a real disagreement

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Let's begin. Bao, the plots.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: We have six vacant plots this season, out of the fifty-two.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: And who's waiting for them?

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: The waitlist is around thirty people now. It's grown a lot.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Thirty? I thought it was under twenty.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Bao, could you check the sheet?

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: You're right, it's seventeen. I was counting people who emailed twice.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Seventeen for six plots is still a long wait.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: Could we split a couple of the big plots in half?

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Some of those plot holders have been here fifteen years. They won't like it.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: They don't use half of it, though. It's all squash.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: That reminds me, the old fence by the gate went up the year I joined. Fifteen years ago.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: I'll offer the six plots to the first six on the list this week.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Good. And splitting plots, we'll leave that for the annual meeting.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: Fine.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Irrigation. Dmitri, you've been pushing the drip system.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: I have. The quote was three thousand dollars, installed.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: That's a lot of money for hoses.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: It's not hoses. It's a timed system. It would cut our water use by half.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: And who maintains the timers once it's in?

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: What did the water cost last summer?

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Twenty-one hundred, from the bill.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: So it pays for itself in a couple of summers.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Can we even afford it right now?

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: The bank balance is fifty-six hundred. We could, but it would leave very little.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: There's a city green-space grant. The deadline is March fifteenth.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: Could the grant cover the whole thing?

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: Most of it. They fund up to seventy-five percent.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Then we apply for the grant and only pay the rest ourselves.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: That's the sensible way. We'll apply for the grant, and install the drip system if we get it.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: I'll write the grant application this weekend and send it round by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Somebody has to show the city photos of the plots. They always want photos.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: I take photos every week anyway. I'll send Dmitri the best ones.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: The spring fair. Holly?

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: May third, rain or shine. And we have fifteen vendors confirmed, which is our best year.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Fifteen. Wonderful.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: Where do they all go? The path by the beds is narrow.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Along the fence, and the food ones in the parking lot.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: The parking lot is where the mayoral debate stage was last fall.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: That debate. Neither of them knew where the garden even was.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: One of them called it a park. A park!

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: So, the parking lot for food. Do we need a permit for that?

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: The church owns the lot. They just want us to clean up after.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Holly, how many vendors have actually paid their fee?

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Oh. Paid? Eleven. The other four said yes but haven't paid.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Then it's eleven confirmed until they pay.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Fine. Eleven confirmed, four likely.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: I'll chase the four unpaid vendors on Friday if you send me their numbers.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: I'll send you the list tonight.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: Who's doing the plant sale table this year?

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: The layout map should go on the shed door so people know where to set up.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Volunteer hours. Eight hours per plot holder, as always.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: Only sixty-four percent did their hours last year.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Then the other third should lose their plots. That's the rule.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: Some of them work nights. They can't come to Saturday work days.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: The rule doesn't say Saturdays. It says eight hours.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: In practice, all the work days are Saturdays.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: What if we had a weekday evening work day once a month?

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: That's fair. Nobody can say we didn't offer.

turns.speaker: Holly
turns.text: Okay, evening work days. But after that, if you don't do your hours, you lose the plot.

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: Then that's the rule: one evening work day a month, and the hours are enforced from June.

turns.speaker: Bao
turns.text: I'll put the evening dates on the shared calendar this week.

turns.speaker: Dmitri
turns.text: Does a plot holder get a warning before they lose the plot?

turns.speaker: Esther
turns.text: A written warning in August, and then a conversation. Nobody loses a plot by email. Thank you all. Good meeting.
